title: Writing: An Essay on an Economic Issue

writingModel.placeholder: State the economic issue and why it matters
writingModel.hint: Use economic vocabulary: "the distribution of…", "inequality in…", "the regulation of…"

writingModel.placeholder: First argument — economic evidence or principle
writingModel.hint: Use word families: "productively / productivity / production / producer"
Use "although / however / on the other hand" + economic vocabulary

writingModel.placeholder: Analysis — what the evidence shows about trade-offs
writingModel.hint: Hedging: "suggests that / may indicate / it is possible that"
"What the evidence suggests is…" / "It is clear that sustainable / affordable / equitable solutions require…"

writingTemplate.prefix: The ___ of income and wealth is one of the most debated ___ issues of our time.
Evidence suggests that high ___ reduces ___ and undermines social ___.
writingTemplate.hint: Three nouns from different word families

writingTemplate.prefix: However, ___ of market-generated inequality argue that ___ rewards create ___.
The evidence ___ suggests that ___ redistribution can coexist with strong ___.
What is clear is that ___ and ___ solutions are both ___ and ___ necessary.

items: The distribution of income and wealth…
Investment in infrastructure and education…
The regulation of financial markets…
The productivity of workers depends on…
Unemployment and underemployment affect…
Economically sustainable policies…
Financially accessible services…
Globally competitive industries…
Politically feasible reforms…
Socially productive investment…
Unregulated markets tend to produce externalities.
Underdeveloped economies need investment.
Overproduction leads to falling prices.
Underinvestment in public services has long-term costs.
Macroeconomic stability is a prerequisite for microeconomic growth.
The evidence strongly suggests that redistribution is not incompatible with growth.
Sustainable and affordable solutions are achievable with political will.
Inequality is neither irreversible nor inevitable — policy choices matter.
What is needed is economically informed and socially equitable reform.
An unequal society is ultimately an inefficient and unstable one.

questions.text: "The ___ of income affects consumption patterns across the economy." (distribute → noun)
"___ solutions are ones that can be maintained without depleting future resources." (sustain → adjective)
"High ___ is associated with lower economic growth." (equal → opposite noun)
questions.hint: in- + equal → inequality (the state of being unequal)

questions.text: "Markets need careful ___ to prevent externalities from harming society." (regulate → noun)
"___ policies ignore the need for long-term investment in public services." (short + sight → adjective)
questions.hint: short-sighted = failing to consider future consequences (compound adjective)

questions.text: "High ___ means people cannot afford basic necessities." (equal → negative adjective)
"The ___ of currencies can destabilise financial markets." (de- + value → noun)
questions.hint: devalue → devaluation (-tion suffix: the act of devaluing)
